summary: Merge integration defect found by the author before review: dev's device-id floor (detail::refuse_unsafe_device_id_a4, #7811) returns a 400 on the live route before this branch sets its outcome word, so the refusal was counted `internal` (the word for an unexpected exception). Owner ruling (questions window, 2026-11-25): add a 32nd word. Fixed in f86f240b16: LiveOutcome::kBadDeviceId / bad_device_id (appended, index 31), set on the guard's early return; 192 series; REST test (400, no audit row, no dispatch, counted under the requested kind or unknown). Re-reviewed at governance (security, architect, cpp-safety, cpp-expert, quality, sre, consistency: clean).

Unescaped `|` in `error|` inside two markdown table rows (mcp.md get_device_live row, upgrading.md live-read table row 32) split the cell in a GFM render and dropped the rest of the row (Errors/Metrics/Permission). Originated in this branch's G-UP-1 docs, not in the merge. Escaped as `error\|` in the follow-up commit.

The routed observability paragraph omitted the new word and its REST/MCP asymmetry and kept the rationale 'the closed set has no word for it' for the uncounted MCP shape refusal, now false; mcp-server.md and the mcp_server.cpp comment carried the same rationale. Reworded in all three (the MCP handler validates before it arms an outcome; the REST route counts its own device-id refusal as bad_device_id); rest-api.md live route Errors list, reason-less list and metric word examples also name the word and the id 400.

Stale counts after the 32nd word: ADR-1005 (31 words), docs/test-coverage.md (the ruled 31). Found by cpp-expert, sre, docs-writer, consistency-auditor and architect. Corrected, with a dated note naming bad_device_id.

The MCP agent_id bound is 256 BYTES (code, REST floor) but mcp.md, mcp-server.md and the tool's refusal text said characters; metrics.md said the MCP tool refuses 'the same ids' where it refuses a superset (empty, __all__, DEL); the OpenAPI 400 text for the live route named only the control byte, not the over-256-byte arm. All reworded (bytes; superset stated; OpenAPI 400 says over 256 bytes or a byte below 0x20 and bad_device_id).

Nothing locked that the MCP surface never counts bad_device_id (the control-byte case is counted under kind uptime, not unknown, so the existing assertions are vacuous for it); the REST test did not pin the 257-byte arm or the unserved-kind label for processes; a case title still said three late tokens. Added the MCP bad_device_id == 0 checks over all kinds, a 257-byte REST case under kind=processes (and no scoped-gate ask), and retitled the case.

The MCP get_device_live handler carries its own copy of the device-id floor instead of calling dev's refuse_unsafe_agent_id / auth::agent_id_is_audit_safe ('never copy this predicate into a route'). It is a strict superset (also empty, __all__, DEL), runs before any row that carries the id and writes no audit row, so it is stricter than the shared floor today; drift risk only. Documented at the site as a deliberate superset to update with the shared predicate; not refactored (the -32602 message text would change).

Dev's shared floor (auth::is_audit_safe_bytes) admits DEL (0x7f), which the MCP tool refuses: a DEL byte in a REST path id reaches target_id and the gates. DEL is not a log-injection byte (CR, LF, TAB are); audit_token/log_token apply at the sinks. Not widened on this branch (one shared predicate, never forked). Follow-up for the owner of the shared floor.
disposition: deferred-to-issue #TBD (shared device-id floor: add DEL (0x7f) to auth::is_audit_safe_bytes, and have get_device_live call it)
